paper.title: Identifying Best Interventions through Online Importance Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Best soft intervention identification with fixed sample budget T and cost budget B (S2), probability of error
unmapped: Arms are soft interventions P_k(V|pa(V)) in a causal graph; the learner knows these conditionals and the marginal of pa(V) (hence the divergences M_kj) and observes (Y, V, pa(V)), enabling importance sampling across arms (information leakage)
Average cost constraint on the sampling fractions: sum_k c_k nu_k <= B, with known per-arm costs c_k
Conditionals assumed mutually absolutely continuous; V, pa(V) discrete
settings.definition_quote: The $K$ different soft interventions can be thought of as the $K$ \textit{arms} of a bandit problem. Let the reward of arm $k$ be denoted by: $\mu_k = \EE_{k} \left[ Y \right]$ ... We assume that there is only one best arm. ... Cost Budget (S2): ... It is required that the average cost of sampling does not exceed a cost budget $B$ .ie. $\sum_{k = 0}^{K-1} c_k \nu_k \leq B.$

settings.name_in_paper: Best soft intervention identification with fixed sample budget T and cost budget B (S2), simple regret
unmapped: Arms are soft interventions P_k(V|pa(V)) in a causal graph; the learner knows these conditionals and the marginal of pa(V) (hence the divergences M_kj) and observes (Y, V, pa(V)), enabling importance sampling across arms (information leakage)
Average cost constraint on the sampling fractions: sum_k c_k nu_k <= B, with known per-arm costs c_k
Conditionals assumed mutually absolutely continuous; V, pa(V) discrete
settings.definition_quote: The simple regret is given by $r(T,B) = \sum _{k \neq k^*}\Delta_k\PP \left( \hat{k}(T,B) = k\right)$.

algorithms.name: Successive Rejects with Importance Sampling v1 (SRISv1)
Successive Rejects with Importance Sampling v2 (SRISv2)

symbols.H_bar: max_{k != k*} log2(10/Delta_k)^3 (sigma*(B, R*(Delta_k))/Delta_k)^2, with sigma* the effective standard deviation from the allocation LP
symbols.logbar_n: harmonic number sum_{i=1}^{n(T)} 1/i with n(T) = ceil(log 2 * log 10 sqrt(T))

source.label: mainresult
source.quote: Let $\Delta= \min \limits_{k \neq k*} \Delta_k$. ... The probability of error for Algorithm \ref{alg:pickbest} satisfies: e(T,B) \leq 2K^2 \log_2 (20/\Delta) \exp \left( - \frac{T}{ 2\bar{H} \overline{\log}(n(T))} \right) when the budget for the total number of samples is $T$ and $\Delta \geq 10/\sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Also proved as part 2 of Theorem 5 (thm:detailed), where H_bar is written equivalently via v* = 1/sigma*, with a factor 10^2 inside (Delta_k/10)^2: Theorem 5 defines H_bar with (Delta_k/10)^2, i.e. 100x larger than Theorem 1's expression; recorded as in Theorem 1. The quantity is a probability of error.

bound.regime: sum restricted to suboptimal arms with Delta_i >= 10/sqrt(T)

symbols.I_small: indicator that some suboptimal arm has Delta_k < 10/sqrt(T)
symbols.H_bar_i: max_{l: Delta_l >= Delta_i} log2(10/Delta_l)^3 / ((Delta_l/10)^2 v*(B, R*(Delta_l))^2)
symbols.logbar_n: harmonic number sum_{i=1}^{n(T)} 1/i with n(T) = ceil(log 2 * log 10 sqrt(T))

source.label: mainresult2
source.quote: The simple regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:pickbest} when the number of samples is $T$ satisfies: r(T,B) \leq \frac{10}{\sqrt{T}}\mathds{1} \left\{\exists k\neq k^* \text{ s.t } \Delta_k < 10/\sqrt{T} \right\} +2K^2\sum_{k \neq k^*: \Delta_k \geq 10/\sqrt{T}} \Delta_k \log_2\left(\frac{20}{\Delta_k}\right) \exp \left( - \frac{T}{ 2\bar{H}_{k} \overline{\log}(n(T))} \right)

results.notes: The sum is only over suboptimal arms with Delta_k >= 10/sqrt(T); sum_subopt cannot express this restriction, so it is noted in the regime. Also proved as part 1 of Theorem 5.
